questions.question: In a grade 1 ligament sprain, pain and swelling are:

options.A: Mild with little or no tear

questions.explanation: Grade 1 is a stretch of fibres with minimal tearing and no instability.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In a grade 2 ligament sprain, pain and swelling are typically:
questions.explanation: Grade 2 is a partial tear with moderate pain and swelling and mild to moderate laxity.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In a grade 3 ligament sprain, pain and swelling are typically:
questions.explanation: Grade 3 is complete rupture with marked instability.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Decalcification (softening) of bones is the feature of:
questions.explanation: Osteomalacia is defective mineralisation of osteoid in adults, usually from vitamin D deficiency.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Abnormal collagen synthesis is the basic defect in:
questions.explanation: OI results from mutations in the type I collagen genes, causing brittle bones.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Complex regional pain syndrome type 2 differs from type 1 in being:

options.A: Associated with a definable nerve injury

questions.explanation: CRPS 1 (RSD) follows trauma without nerve injury; CRPS 2 (causalgia) follows a nerve lesion.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In a Colles fracture the distal radial fragment is displaced:
questions.explanation: Colles fracture: dorsal displacement and tilt of the distal radius (dinner-fork deformity).
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In a Smith's (reverse Colles) fracture the distal radial fragment is displaced:
questions.explanation: Smith's fracture results from a fall on the back of the flexed wrist, with the fragment displaced volarly (garden spade deformity).
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A garden spade deformity of the wrist is characteristic of:
questions.explanation: Smith's fracture produces a garden spade deformity, whereas Colles gives a dinner-fork deformity.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Osgood-Schlatter disease is traction apophysitis at the:
questions.explanation: It affects adolescent athletes with quadriceps pull on the tibial tuberosity.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Coxa vara is a femoral neck-shaft angle:

options.C: Less than the normal 125 degrees (below about 120)

questions.explanation: Coxa vara reduces the neck-shaft angle; coxa valga increases it above about 135 degrees.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Coxa valga is a femoral neck-shaft angle:
questions.explanation: In coxa valga the neck-shaft angle exceeds normal and the limb appears lengthened.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The correct sequence of fracture healing is:

options.A: Haematoma, granulation tissue (inflammation), callus formation, consolidation, remodelling
options.B: Callus formation, remodelling, consolidation, haematoma, granulation tissue
options.D: Haematoma, consolidation, callus formation, remodelling, granulation

questions.explanation: Fracture healing follows inflammation, soft and hard callus, consolidation and finally remodelling.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In Pauwels' classification of femoral neck fractures, an angle of the fracture line to the horizontal of less than 30 degrees is:
questions.explanation: Type 1 (under 30 degrees) is the most stable; type 3 (over 50 degrees) is vertical and the most unstable.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In Pauwels' classification, a fracture line angle of 30-50 degrees to the horizontal is:
questions.explanation: Type 2 lies between 30 and 50 degrees.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In Pauwels' classification, a fracture line angle of more than 50 degrees to the horizontal is:
questions.explanation: A more vertical line gives greater shear forces and a higher risk of non-union.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Garden stage 1 of femoral neck fracture is:
questions.explanation: Garden I is an incomplete or impacted fracture; stages III-IV carry high risk of avascular necrosis.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Garden stage 2 of femoral neck fracture is:
questions.explanation: Garden II: complete fracture without displacement.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Garden stage 3 of femoral neck fracture is:
questions.explanation: Garden III: complete with partial displacement (trabecular malalignment).
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Garden stage 4 of femoral neck fracture is:
questions.explanation: Garden IV: total displacement; the head is free of the neck.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which Garden stages are considered stable and are usually treated with internal fixation?
questions.explanation: Undisplaced stages I and II are stable and fixed with screws; displaced stages III-IV often need arthroplasty in the elderly.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In Evans' classification of intertrochanteric fractures, a type 1 fracture is:

options.A: A 3-part displaced fracture with posterolateral comminution
options.C: A 4-part fracture with comminution of both trochanters

questions.explanation: Evans type 1: undisplaced two-part fracture.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In Evans' classification, a type 2 intertrochanteric fracture is:

options.C: A 3-part displaced fracture with posteromedial comminution

questions.explanation: Evans type 2: displaced two-part fracture.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In Evans' classification, a type 3 intertrochanteric fracture is:

options.A: A 3-part displaced fracture with posteromedial comminution
options.C: A 3-part displaced fracture with a posterolateral comminuted fragment
options.D: A 4-part fracture with both trochanters comminuted

questions.explanation: Evans type 3: three-part fracture lacking posterolateral support (greater trochanter fragment).
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In Evans' classification, a type 4 intertrochanteric fracture is:

options.A: A 3-part displaced fracture with a posteromedial comminution

questions.explanation: Evans type 4: three-part fracture lacking medial support (lesser trochanter fragment).
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In Evans' classification, a type 5 intertrochanteric fracture is:

options.B: A 4-part displaced fracture with comminution of both trochanters

questions.explanation: Evans type 5 is the most unstable pattern.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A minimal tear of the anterior talofibular ligament is graded as ankle sprain:
questions.explanation: Grade 1: stretch or minimal tear of the ATFL with minimal functional loss.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A partial tear of the anterior talofibular and calcaneofibular ligaments with some functional loss is graded as ankle sprain:
questions.explanation: Grade 2 involves partial tears of the ATFL and CFL with moderate swelling and some loss of function.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A complete tear of the ATFL and CFL with some tear of the posterior talofibular ligament and total functional loss is graded as ankle sprain:
questions.explanation: Grade 3 is complete disruption of the lateral ligament complex.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In Jackson's zone of coagulation, the cells are:
questions.explanation: The central zone is irreversibly necrotic.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In Jackson's zone of stasis, the cells are:

options.D: Injured but may die within 24-48 hours if no treatment is given

questions.explanation: The zone of stasis is salvageable with good resuscitation.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In Jackson's zone of hyperaemia, the cell injury is:
questions.explanation: The outer zone recovers spontaneously.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: According to the Rule of Nines, which of the following statements is FALSE?

options.C: Anterior and posterior trunk are 18% each
options.D: Each arm is 18% of body surface area

questions.explanation: Each arm is 9% of the body surface area.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The inflammatory phase of wound healing lasts about:
questions.explanation: Inflammation dominates the first 3-5 days.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The proliferative phase of wound healing lasts about:
questions.explanation: Granulation tissue and epithelialisation occur over about 3 weeks.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The maturation (remodelling) phase of wound healing lasts from about:
questions.explanation: Remodelling continues from about a week up to 2 years.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Re-epithelialisation of a wound begins:
questions.explanation: Epithelial cells begin migrating across the wound within about 24 hours.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Wound contraction occurs mainly during the ______ phase of healing.
questions.explanation: Myofibroblasts contract the wound during the proliferative phase.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which statement about a keloid scar is FALSE?

options.A: It is commonly seen in dark-skinned individuals
options.C: It stays within the boundaries of the original wound

questions.explanation: Keloids extend beyond the wound margins; hypertrophic scars stay within them.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A burn with 15% second-degree burn and less than 2% third-degree burn is classified as:
questions.explanation: Minor burns involve under 15% (partial) and under 2% (full) thickness in adults.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A burn with 15-30% second-degree burn and less than 10% third-degree burn is classified as:
questions.explanation: Moderate burns are 15-25% (partial) and under 10% (full) thickness in adults.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A burn with 30% second-degree burn and 10% third-degree burn is classified as:
questions.explanation: Major burns exceed 25% partial or 10% full-thickness involvement.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A pink or red burn wound is seen in:
questions.explanation: Superficial burns are red, dry and painful without blisters.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A mixed red or waxy white appearance of the burn wound is seen in:
questions.explanation: Deep dermal burns are mottled red and white.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The dermis is involved in all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: First-degree burns involve only the epidermis.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Spontaneous healing is expected in:
questions.explanation: Epidermal burns re-epithelialise from the intact basal layer.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Skin grafting is necessary in:
questions.explanation: Full-thickness burns have no epithelial elements left and need grafting.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Normal sensitivity to pain, touch and temperature is retained in:
questions.explanation: Nerve endings are destroyed in deeper burns.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A charred appearance of the wound is seen in:
questions.explanation: Fourth-degree burns involve muscle and bone and look charred.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding burn healing times is FALSE?

options.A: A full-thickness burn heals spontaneously in 21-35 days
options.B: Superficial partial-thickness burn heals in 5-21 days
options.D: Deep partial-thickness burn heals in 21-35 days

questions.explanation: Full-thickness burns cannot re-epithelialise except from the margins and need grafting.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: When skin from another species is used for grafting, it is called a:
questions.explanation: A xenograft (heterograft) comes from another species, e.g. pig skin.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: When skin from the same species (another person) is used for grafting, it is called an:
questions.explanation: An allograft (homograft) is from a donor of the same species.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The common deformity seen if the anterior neck is involved in a burn is:
questions.explanation: Anterior neck burns contract into flexion; the neck is held in extension to prevent this.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The common deformity seen if the shoulder is involved in a burn is:
questions.explanation: Axillary burns draw the arm into adduction with internal rotation.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The common deformity seen if the elbow is involved in a burn is:
questions.explanation: The elbow tends to flex and pronate.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The common deformity seen if the hip is involved in a burn is:
questions.explanation: Hip burns lead to flexion and adduction contractures.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The common deformity seen if the knee is involved in a burn is:
questions.explanation: Posterior knee burns cause knee flexion contracture.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The common deformity seen if the foot is involved in a burn is:
questions.explanation: The foot tends to plantar flex (equinus), so a splint holds it at neutral.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The intrinsic-plus (safe) position given to patients with a burn injury of the hand is:

options.A: 30 degrees wrist flexion with MCP extension
options.B: 15 degrees wrist extension, 70 degrees MCP flexion, PIP and DIP flexion
options.C: 15 degrees wrist extension, 70 degrees MCP flexion, PIP and DIP extension and thumb abduction
options.D: 15 degrees wrist flexion, 70 degrees MCP flexion, PIP and DIP extension

questions.explanation: The safe position keeps the collateral ligaments stretched and prevents claw deformity.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Compression garments used to reduce hypertrophic scarring exert a pressure of about:
questions.explanation: Effective pressure is about 24-30 mm Hg; sustained pressure above capillary pressure risks ischaemia.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A healthy red wound contains:
questions.explanation: A red wound has healthy granulation tissue and is in the proliferative phase.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A yellow wound contains:
questions.explanation: Yellow tissue is stringy, moist fibrin slough.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A black wound contains:
questions.explanation: Black wounds have dry necrotic tissue (eschar) requiring debridement.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The main treatment goal for a healthy red wound is:
questions.explanation: Red wounds are protected and kept moist to support granulation.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The main treatment goal for a black wound is:
questions.explanation: Eschar delays healing and must be removed.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In vacuum-assisted closure (negative pressure wound therapy) the pressure applied is:
questions.explanation: NPWT usually applies about -125 mm Hg suction.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Hyperbaric oxygen therapy is contraindicated in all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Osteomyelitis is an indication for HBOT.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: An irrigation pressure range of ______ is considered safe for wound irrigation.
questions.explanation: Pressures of 4-15 psi cleanse without driving bacteria into tissue.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a contraindication for enzymatic debridement?
questions.explanation: Enzymatic debridement works on moist necrotic tissue.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following dressings can be used in an infected wound?
questions.explanation: Occlusive dressings are avoided in infected wounds, whereas gauze allows inspection and drainage.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following statements is FALSE?

options.A: Alginates are not recommended for dry wounds
options.B: Hydrogels are not recommended in heavily exudative wounds
options.C: Hydrocolloids are recommended for wounds with heavy exudate and tracts
options.D: Hydrogels and foams are used for partial and full thickness wounds

questions.explanation: Hydrocolloids absorb little and are unsuitable for heavy exudate or deep tracts.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following statements is TRUE?

options.A: Alginates are used in dry, uninfected wounds
options.B: Hydrocolloids do not support autolytic debridement
options.C: Foams must be changed every 2 hours
options.D: Transparent films are used in stage 1 and 2 ulcers

questions.explanation: Films protect superficial, minimally exuding wounds.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which statement regarding a rigid post-operative dressing like POP is FALSE?

options.A: Application requires a professional skill set
options.B: Daily changing of the dressing is not possible
options.C: Immediate inspection of the wound is possible

questions.explanation: A rigid dressing hides the wound, so inspection needs a window or removal.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which statement regarding a soft post-operative dressing (Ace wrap, shrinker) is FALSE?

options.A: The risk of a tourniquet effect is negligible
options.B: The risk of contracture is high
options.C: There is no control over the amount of tension in the bandage

questions.explanation: Poorly applied elastic wraps can act as a tourniquet.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: For transfemoral amputations, the elastic wrap should be at least:
questions.explanation: A wider (6-inch) bandage is required to wrap the thigh and hip.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
